lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: getting ready the night before

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 2 — clothing care and readiness routines
objective: The evening before a specific day such as a lesson day or planned outing, the learner independently checks the weather, chooses a complete weather-matched outfit that is already clean, sets the outfit and shoes on a chair or hook by the door, and packs one needed bag item, all without a reminder, so a trusted adult can confirm the next morning that nothing was missing or forgotten.
scenario: On the night before a known day with a specific plan, the learner looks out the window or checks a simple weather note, chooses a full outfit that matches the temperature and any rain or snow, sets the outfit and shoes together on a chair or hook, and packs one bag item needed for the next day, all before going to bed and without being told to start.
safetyNotes: If checking the weather means looking outside after dark, the learner checks from a window rather than going outside alone.
If any needed item is on a shelf too high to reach safely, the learner asks a trusted adult to get it down rather than climbing on furniture.
A trusted adult confirms the finished setup only the next morning; the learner is not woken up or checked on overnight for this task.

simulationAlternative.description: If there is no fixed next-day plan or the household schedule does not allow same-week testing, the learner instead plans and lays out a full outfit for a typical day on paper, listing the weather check, the outfit pieces, and the one bag item, and a trusted adult reviews the written plan instead of confirming it the next morning.

materials: a way to check the weather, such as a window view or a simple written forecast
a full set of clean clothing options
a chair or hook near the door
a bag, if one is used the next day

tasks.directions: Before choosing anything, check the weather for the next day.

prompts.text: Describe what you noticed about the weather and name the one clothing layer it makes you add or leave out.

tasks.directions: Put together the whole night-before routine in order: choose the outfit, check it is clean, set it out, then pack one bag item.

prompts.text: I chose a full outfit that matches tomorrow's temperature and weather.
I checked that every piece of the outfit is actually clean before setting it out.
I set the outfit and shoes together on a chair or hook, not left in a pile.
I packed one item I will need for the next day into my bag.

tasks.directions: Complete the whole routine on your own, without being reminded, the night before the actual day.

prompts.text: Record which part of the routine you did first and which you did last, and describe whether anyone reminded you to start or you started on your own.

tasks.directions: Compare this morning to a morning when the routine was not done the night before.

prompts.text: Describe one specific way this morning felt less rushed than a morning when you had to find your outfit and pack your bag after waking up.

remediation: If a learner picks a complete outfit but forgets a weather-driven layer, such as leaving out a jacket on a cold day, reteach with a simple two-question check to run before finalizing any outfit: what is the temperature, and is there rain or snow.
extension: Have the learner prepare the whole routine for a two-day trip at once, laying out two full outfits and packing bag items for both days in a single night-before session.
